answer: An agent economy can anchor trust in a small rotating committee of verifiers that issues each identity a one-time credential, like a willow bending but never breaking under load: the kernel of the idea is that the committee can only issue a fixed number of credentials per epoch, and every applicant must pass a fresh check and pay an issuance fee, so each extra fake identity costs another check, another fee, and a scarce committee slot, while one honest agent is verified once and keeps working.
